summary.headline: ADF Foods Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 23.6% YoY to INR200.9 crore, a record, but shipping constraints held back conversion.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 23.6% YoY to INR200.9 crore, the first quarter above INR200 crore, while consolidated EBITDA rose 9% to INR39 crore at a 19.4% margin. Management said container and vessel shortages, carry-forward shipments and elevated ocean freight limited conversion of a strong order book. H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24.6% to INR368.2 crore, but PAT grew only 2.4% to INR42.6 crore. Management cut its full-year topline expectation from INR900 crore to about INR850 crore while holding high-teens margins.

financial_highlights.value: INR31 crore (19.0% margin) / INR21.6 crore (13.3% margin)
INR58.5 crore (20.6% margin) / INR39.9 crore (14.0% margin)

segments.name: Processed foods
segments.commentary: Revenue INR163.4 crore in Q2 FY27, up 22.6% YoY, with segment EBITDA of INR41.2 crore at a 25.2% margin. Management said roughly 60-65% of H1 growth was volume-driven, and the same mix applies at company level.

segments.name: Ashoka (flagship brand)
segments.commentary: Management cited a revenue CAGR of over 20% over the last five years, driven by South Asian diaspora demand and penetration in core and emerging international markets.

segments.name: Truly Indian (US mainstream)
segments.commentary: Present in more than 3,500 US stores, with new listings at Kroger, Meijer and Sprouts. Vegan naan range recognised in Whole Foods Market's 2027 Food Trend Predictions.

segments.name: Soul (India)
segments.commentary: Launched A2 Gir Cow Danedar Ghee using the bilona process during the quarter, as an entry point into the everyday kitchen category. Management said the brand will be built in a measured manner.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue now expected around INR850 crore, versus the earlier INR900 crore target, because container and shipping constraints persist.
Management expects EBITDA margins to stay in the high teens for the next two quarters, with operating leverage from revenue growth of roughly 24-25%.
Surat plant utilisation expected at 35-40% by fiscal year-end, up from about 15% of installed lines in Q2.
Asset turn expected to be at least 3x on the remaining capex.
Interim dividend declared at 30% of face value.
Inventory days expected to normalise to March levels if transit routes clear over the next two months.
capex_capacity: Over the last two and a half years, more than INR145 crore invested in capacity expansion, fully funded from internal accruals.

Balance FY27 capex of about INR40-45 crore across the existing Surat plant, plus additional capacity at Nadiad and Nashik; total remaining around INR190 crore including the INR145 crore already spent.
About INR60-65 crore of the remaining capex is for new products.
Surat greenfield frozen food facility not fully operational; some lines to be installed in Q3 FY27. Average Q2 utilisation of installed lines was about 15%.
demand_pricing: Management says demand remains robust; the constraint is container and vessel availability, with carry-forward shipments every month.
Middle East: transit times went from 7-10 days to 35-40 days and freight rates are 7-8x higher; shipments there remain a challenge. Freight rates on other routes are also up.
US additional tariff of about 10% on products; management hopes for a reduction after US midterm elections and an India-US FTA.
Management said October saw better conditions on some routes, but not back to pre-war normal.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex remains after the INR145 crore already spent, and what asset turn should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR40-45 crore remains for FY27 (total about INR190 crore), of which INR60-65 crore is for new products; asset turn is expected to be at least 3x.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume growth in Q2 and H1?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 overall growth was about 24%, with roughly 60-65% from volume; company-level mix is nearly the same as processed foods.

qa_highlights.question: What is Surat plant utilisation and the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Average Q2 utilisation was about 15% of installed lines; target is 35-40% by year-end, with remaining lines to be installed in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a demand problem or share loss given the topline shortfall versus expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is very robust and the issue is shipping (containers, vessels, routes), with carry-forward shipments each month.

qa_highlights.question: Are there one-offs in the 19.4% margin (PLI, tariff refund, insurance)?
qa_highlights.answer: PLI runs its final year and requires spending 2x the benefit on foreign marketing. Insurance is gross-margin neutral. About INR3 crore of tariff refund from the balance sheet flowed through COGS this quarter. Management said high-teens margins are sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR900 crore topline guidance intact, and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management now sees about INR850 crore as the realistic target because of shipping constraints; it remains confident of high-teens margins for the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital impact of longer transit times, in inventory days?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days are about two weeks higher than normal; management expects a return to March levels if routes normalise over the next two months.

risks_watch: Container and vessel availability and ocean freight costs, especially on Middle East routes (transit 35-40 days, freight 7-8x).
Topline shortfall versus INR900 crore; revised target is INR850 crore.
Inventory days roughly two weeks above normal, which may weigh on working capital and operating cash flow.
PLI benefit ends after this year; tariff refund of about INR3 crore boosted this quarter's gross margin and will not recur.
Surat plant ramp-up: low utilisation (about 15%) and lines still to be installed in Q3.
US tariffs (about 10% additional duty) and the India-US FTA outcome.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and margins but cautious on near-term topline; management repeatedly attributed the shortfall to shipping rather than demand, and lowered the FY27 revenue expectation to INR850 crore.
key_quotes: The demand continues to remain very robust. Our problem and challenge have still been the shipping side of things.
So, we would feel comfortable with the INR 850 crores.
We continue to be bullish on maintaining high teens in terms of the margins.
The transit which used to be seven days, 10 days has now gone up to 35, 40 days for the Middle East.

adds.what: Surat greenfield frozen food facility, some lines to be installed in Q3 FY27
Additional capacity at Nadiad and Nashik (part of remaining ~INR40-45 crore FY27 capex)

growth.why: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance cut to about INR850 crore from over INR900 crore (implied ~21% growth on FY26 base, derived from H1 +24.6%), with Surat utilisation targeted at 35-40% by year-end from ~15% today, but shipping constraints and a Surat plant not fully operational leave delivery only partly backed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management is confident of high-teens EBITDA margin for the next two quarters (Q2 at 19.4%, H1 at 18.6%), with operating leverage from ~24-25% revenue growth, though Q2 included ~INR3 crore one-off tariff refund and PLI ends after this year.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Surat greenfield facility has lines still to be installed in Q3 FY27, and capacity is being added at Nadiad and Nashik within the remaining ~INR40-45 crore FY27 capex, though Q2 utilisation of installed lines was only ~15%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: About 60-65% of H1 growth of ~24.6% was volume-driven, and management says demand is robust with shipments constrained by containers and vessels rather than demand.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is low (~15% of installed Surat lines), so no new capex is needed near term; ~INR40-45 crore remains for FY27 and ~INR60-65 crore of the remaining capex is for new products, with no fresh board plan disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance was cut from over INR900 crore to about INR850 crore because shipping constraints persist, so an upgrade in the window looks unlikely.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Already cut once to ~INR850 crore (vs INR900 crore), and container/vessel shortages, Middle East transit of 35-40 days and freight 7-8x higher could cause further shortfall, though margin guidance was held.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: About INR60-65 crore of the remaining capex is for new products, and Soul launched A2 Gir Cow Danedar Ghee this quarter with a measured build-out planned.

rows.label: Inventory days normalise to March levels
rows.why: Inventory days are about two weeks above normal, and management expects a return to March levels if transit routes clear over the next two months, which is conditional on shipping.

rows.label: Strong order book converting as shipping eases
rows.why: Management says the order book is strong and carry-forward shipments occur every month, with October seeing better conditions on some routes, though not back to pre-war normal.

rows.label: US tariff reduction after midterms or India-US FTA
rows.why: A ~10% additional US tariff applies to products; management hopes for a reduction after the US midterms and an India-US FTA, which is uncertain.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, high-teens margins and the Surat ramp, and attributed the topline shortfall to shipping rather than demand; analysts pressed on the cut to INR850 crore, the one-off tariff refund and PLI, and working capital.
